Income tax in Qatar (2026): how much of your salary do you keep?

Qatar charges no personal income tax on employment income, so an expat on QAR 240,000 a year keeps the full QAR 240,000. A Qatari national pays 7% of salary into the GRSIA pension fund, QAR 16,800 on the same pay, and keeps QAR 223,200. The employer adds 14% on top for nationals, and expats receive an end-of-service gratuity instead of a pension.

What the law says

The figures are the 2026 rules as the calculator models them. Salary is not taxed for individuals in Qatar. What differs by person is the pension: Qatari nationals contribute through the General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority (GRSIA), and expats do not.

No personal income tax on salary

Qatar does not tax wages, allowances or bonuses for an individual, so there is no tax bracket and no tax withheld from your payslip. VAT, where a country charges it, is a consumption tax added to what you buy and is not taken from your pay, so it is not part of this calculation.

GRSIA pension for Qatari nationals

The calculator takes 7% of pay from Qatari nationals for the GRSIA pension, on pay up to QAR 100,000 a month. The employer pays 14% on top. The employer share is shown as a cost and does not reduce your pay.

Who paysRateCap
Employee (national)7%QAR 100,000 a month
Employer14%QAR 100,000 a month

Expats: no pension, an end-of-service gratuity

Expatriates do not contribute to GRSIA. The employer owes an end-of-service gratuity at the end of the contract, based on basic pay and years of service under the labour law. It is paid once, when you leave.

Sources

  • General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority (GRSIA), pension contributions for nationals
  • General Tax Authority, Qatar, taxes in Qatar

How much income tax does an expat pay in Qatar on QAR 240,000?

An expat on QAR 240,000 pays no income tax and no pension contribution, so take-home pay is QAR 240,000, or 100% of gross. A raise is kept in full because the marginal rate is 0%.

Take-home pay for a Qatari national on QAR 240,000 after GRSIA

A Qatari national on QAR 240,000 pays no income tax but 7% into the GRSIA pension, QAR 16,800 a year. You keep QAR 223,200, or 93.0% of gross. The employer pays a further 14%, QAR 33,600, on top, which goes into the pension and does not come out of your pay.

  1. Gross paya year, before taxQAR 240,000
  2. No personal income tax on employmentfor informationQAR 0
  3. GRSIA pension (7%, cap 100,000 a month)contribution, taken from pay−QAR 16,800
  4. Employer 14%, on toppaid by the employer, on topQAR 33,600
  5. Take-home pay93.0% of gross, QAR 18,600 a monthQAR 223,200

The 7% is a pension contribution rather than a tax. It applies up to the cap of QAR 100,000 a month.

How to pay less tax, legally

These are mainstream, legal ways to handle your pay and tax position.

Check your home-country tax residency before you move

Suits: every expat. Zero tax in the Gulf does not always mean zero tax overall: some countries tax citizens on worldwide income, and others treat you as resident until you meet their exit conditions.

Caveat: the rules sit in your home country's law, not in the Gulf state's. Ask your home tax authority or an adviser, and keep records of your move.

Save and invest the extra take-home yourself

Suits: expats who keep the whole salary. Without a pension deduction, retirement saving is your own job. Regular contributions to a pension or investment plan in your home country or a low-cost portfolio are the usual route.

Caveat: a gratuity at the end of the contract is not a retirement plan, and where you invest decides the tax on the returns. Use the Financial Freedom Calculator to see how much you need.

Understand your gratuity before you sign

Suits: expats comparing offers. The gratuity is your only employer-funded exit benefit, and it depends on basic pay and length of service.

Caveat: a contract with a low basic salary and large allowances can produce a smaller gratuity, so ask how it is calculated.

What the calculator does not model

  • Employment income only. It models one salary for a full year, with no other income, bonuses or a part year.
  • Gratuity not modelled. End-of-service gratuity depends on your basic pay, length of service and contract, so it is not added to the figures.
  • Home-country tax. The calculator shows only what the Gulf state takes. Your home country may still tax you on worldwide income, depending on its rules and any treaty.
  • You choose the status. The calculator takes national or expat from you and does not test whether you qualify.
  • Package versus cash. The calculator takes the gross pay you enter. Housing, schooling or flight allowances in your contract are not split out.

General information, not tax advice. The figures follow the rules as published for the year shown. Check the ones that matter to you with the tax authority or an adviser before you sign a contract.

Frequently asked questions

How much tax do I pay on QAR 240,000 in Qatar?

An expat pays no income tax and keeps QAR 240,000. A Qatari national pays 7% into GRSIA and keeps QAR 223,200. Try your own figure in the Global Income Tax Calculator.

What is end-of-service gratuity in Qatar and does it replace a pension?

For expats, yes in practice. They are not in the GRSIA pension scheme, so the employer instead pays a lump sum at the end of the contract, based on basic pay and years of service under the labour law. The money is paid once when you leave, not monthly after retirement. The calculator does not include it, since it depends on your contract.

Why do Qataris pay 7% while the employer pays 14%?

For nationals, GRSIA is funded by shared contributions. The employee pays 7% and the employer 14%, both on pay up to QAR 100,000 a month. Only the 7% reduces your take-home pay. The 14% is paid on top of your salary and is shown separately.

Is there really no income tax in Qatar?

Not on salary. The state does not tax employment income for individuals and there is no personal tax return for wages. Your home country may still tax you under its own rules.

Do I need to pay tax at home if I work in Qatar?

It depends on your home country, which the calculator does not model. Some countries tax citizens on worldwide income or keep you resident for tax for a time. Check with your home tax authority.

What does a Qatar salary buy compared with home?

The Cost of Living Comparator shows what a salary buys in another city, which helps when a package includes housing.
